title: Which of these pairs of angles can make a triangle?
description: Four pairs of angles are added and each sum is compared with one hundred and eighty degrees. A pair makes a triangle only when its sum is less than one hundred and eighty, and the answer is checked with the limit from the example in the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: two angles make a triangle only when they add to less than one hundred and eighty degrees. Watch for students who forget that a sum of exactly one hundred and eighty fails.

source: Determine which of the following pairs can be the angles of a triangle and which cannot: (a) 35°, 150° (b) 70°, 30° (c) 90°, 85° (d) 50°, 150°
video_script.why: The child knows that the arms stop meeting when the two angles reach a sum of one hundred and eighty degrees and now sorts four pairs.
video_script.substitution: Add the two angles and compare the sum with one hundred and eighty degrees.
video_script.anchor: four pairs of angles: thirty five and one hundred and fifty, seventy and thirty, ninety and eighty five, fifty and one hundred and fifty
video_script.payoff_line: The second and third pairs can be the angles of a triangle

final_answer.value: (b) and (c) can be the angles of a triangle; (a) and (d) cannot
final_answer.spoken: the second and third pairs can be the angles of a triangle, and the first and fourth pairs cannot

maths_rules: the arms meet when the sum of the two angles is less than 180°, and do not meet when it is 180° or more
check with the limit: for (a) 180° - 35° = 145° and 150° is more than 145°, cannot; for (c) 180° - 90° = 90° and 85° is less than 90°, can
video_script.design: The four pairs stay in the anchor band. Each pair is added on the board, its sum is placed on a number line with a mark at one hundred and eighty, and the result is checked with the limit.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which pairs can be the angles of a triangle.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, add the two angles in each pair. Thirty five plus one hundred and fifty is one hundred and eighty five.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Seventy plus thirty is one hundred.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Ninety plus eighty five is one hundred and seventy five.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Fifty plus one hundred and fifty is two hundred.

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step two, compare each sum with one hundred and eighty. The first sum is more, so those arms do not meet.
<bookmark mark='b'/>The second sum is less, so those arms meet.
<bookmark mark='c'/>The third sum is less, so those arms meet.
<bookmark mark='d'/>The fourth sum is more, so those arms do not meet.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: check with the limit: (a) 180° - 35° = 145° and 150° is more than 145°;  (c) 180° - 90° = 90° and 85° is less than 90°

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step three, check with the limit. One hundred and eighty minus thirty five is one hundred and forty five. One hundred and fifty is more than that.
<bookmark mark='c'/>One hundred and eighty minus ninety is ninety. Eighty five is less than that.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (b) and (c) can be the angles of a triangle; (a) and (d) cannot
